newsitem.title: UK: Major calls UK Labour's tax pledge ludicrous.
newsitem.headline: Major calls UK Labour's tax pledge ludicrous.

text.p: The main opposition Labour Party's pledge not to raise taxes if it wins Britain's coming general election is "ludicrous," Prime Minister John Major told parliament at question time on Tuesday.
Major said Labour's record on taxes could be judged by the fact that it was the party that last raised Britain's basic tax rate.

He also said Labour, which said on Monday it would not raise either basic-rate or top-rate tax for at least five years if it won power, had never supported the Conservatives' tax cuts or its efforts to restrain public spending.

Major also charged that Labour had plans to increase public spending by 30 billion pounds and said it must disclaim such pledges "if they are up to stand up their ludicrous claim that they would not increase taxes".

In reply to a later questioner, Major said: "The reality is whatever the best intentions of the shadow Chancellor might be, the sheer nature of the Labour Party is that he certainly could not deliver that which he promised." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
